The Philippine government has adopted the name West Philippine Sea to refer to parts of the South China Sea within its territory that are also being claimed by China.

China, the DFA said, should "act responsibly and abide by its obligations under UNCLOS and the final and binding 2016 Arbitral Award."

“We do not even recognize the nine-dash line, much more the 10-dash line,” National Security Adviser Eduardo Año said during the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) press conference on Thursday.

“The arbitral award is final and binding and it gives us our maritime entitlement, our extended economic zone, our territorial waters, and even our extended continental shelf,” he added.

He said that the Philippine government “will do everything in its capacity to ensure that we are protecting our national interest.”

Marcos said that when he took office, his duty was to defend the country's territory.

output.description: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing.

text.preview: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing. The Philippine protest, dated April 5, was posted by the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) as document No. 000228 on April 8. But the Philippine government tarried in filing the protest, doing so two years after Vietnam and Malaysia, and a year after Indonesia. Vietnam and Malaysia filed their protest a day after China submitted its 9-dash line map to the UN on May 7, 2009. Indonesia registered its protest a year ago, even if it did not have a claim on the South China Sea. The map is called “9-dash line” or “9-dotted line” because it shows a series of nine dashes or dotted lines forming a ring around the South China Sea area, which China claims is part of its territory. The area includes the Spratlys group, a cluster of oil-rich islands disputed by five other countries, including the Philippines. China has been using the map with nine dashes in asserting its territorial claim over the whole of the South Sea. But the map first made its way to the UN body, when China used it to challenge the claim made by Vietnam and Malaysia over their extended continental shelves in the South China Sea. The Vietnamese and Malaysian claims were made May 6, 2009; China filed a counter claim using the 9-dash map the next day, May 7. What followed was a series of quick exchanges where Vietnam and Malaysia responded to the Chinese protest. But it would be three months, or August 4, 2009, before the Philippines protested the submissions made by Vietnam and Malaysia. The Philippines’ April 5 2011 protest comes almost two years after its neighbors had raised the issue. text.preview: The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled today that China’s all-encompassing nine-dash line is not valid . (To read the 501-page Award, please go to this site : https://pca-cpa.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/175/2016/07/PH-CN-20160712-Award.pdf ) “The Tribunal found that China’s claim to historic rights to resources was incompatible with the detailed allocation of rights and maritime zones in the Convention and concluded that, to the extent China had historic rights to resources in the waters of the South China Sea, such rights were extinguished by the entry into force of the Convention to the extent they were incompatible with the Convention’s system of maritime zones,” the decision said. The Tribunal concluded that there was no legal basis for China to claim historic rights to resources, in excess of the rights provided for by the Convention, within the sea areas falling within the nine-dash line. China’s nine-dash line map covers almost 80 percent of vast South China Sea, including maritime zones of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. The Tribunal also said the presence of official personnel in high-tide features in the Spratly Islands does not change their legal status as “rocks” that do not generate an exclusive economic zone or continental shelf. China has expanded rocks it is occupying in the disputed Spratlys into artificial islands and built military structures including an airfield. The ruling also applies to the Philippines’ Pag-asa island also known as Thitu island. The Arbitral Tribunal also said China violated the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea by obstructing Philippine vessels going to Scarborough Shoal in April and May 2012 and creating a situation that endangered the ships and personnel. The Court scored China for causing harm to the coral environment by its recent large-scale land reclamation and construction of artificial islands at seven features in the Spratly Islands . output.title: AI says China’s 9-dash line has no legal basis
output.description: Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter).
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter). “The PRC”s nine-dash line in the South China Sea has no legal basis under international law,” said X’s AI tool Grok, referring to China by its official name’s initials. “A 2016 tribunal ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague found it invalid, as it clashes with UNCLOS” or the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The same verdict upheld the Philippines’ sovereign rights over its 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ). “China claims historic rights, but the line, drawn in 1947, overlaps with other nations’ zones, like the Philippines’ EEZ. Tensions keep rising with China’s island-building and militarization,” Grok also wrote. It noted that the nine-dash line became “ten-dash line” after Beijing added another dash east of Taiwan in 1984. It added that China’s expanded claim was “just as baseless – pure geopolitical flexing, not law.” Grok provided the information when asked by Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Commodore Jay Tarriela on his X account. Tarriela is also PCG spokesman on West Philippine Sea issues. “Hey @grok, does PRC have a legal justification of their nine-dash line or ten-dash line in the South China Sea?” asked Tarriela. The PCG official regularly provides updates on coast guard patrols aimed at stopping China’s incursions in the West Philippine Sea. The coast guard’s latest update was last March 9. text.preview:

At a joint press conference with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz, Marcos indicated that the Philippines continued to question China's historical claims.

''We have not rejected any proposals that China has made for us but the premise is something that we question," Marcos said.

articles.title: Philippines rejects new Chinese ‘10-dash line’ map
articles.description: The Philippines on Thursday rejected China's publication of a new map that places nearly the entire South China Sea within its national boundaries, infringing on Manila's claims in the resource-rich waters.

text.preview:
The Philippines on Thursday rejected China's publication of a new map that places nearly the entire South China Sea within its national boundaries, infringing on Manila's claims in the resource-rich waters.

In a statement, the Department of Foreign Affairs said the 2023 edition map is China's latest attempt "to legitimize purported sovereignty and jurisdiction over Philippine features and maritime zones has no basis under international law, particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)."

"The 2016 Arbitral Award invalidated the nine-dashed line. It categorically stated that 'maritime areas of the South China Sea encompassed by the relevant part of the ‘nine-dash line’ are contrary to the Convention and without lawful effect to the extent that they exceed the geographic and substantive limits of China’s maritime entitlements under the Convention,'" the DFA said.

The Philippine government has adopted the name West Philippine Sea to refer to parts of the South China Sea within its territory that are also being claimed by China.

China, the DFA said, should "act responsibly and abide by its obligations under UNCLOS and the final and binding 2016 Arbitral Award."

“We do not even recognize the nine-dash line, much more the 10-dash line,” National Security Adviser Eduardo Año said during the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) press conference on Thursday.

“The arbitral award is final and binding and it gives us our maritime entitlement, our extended economic zone, our territorial waters, and even our extended continental shelf,” he added.

He said that the Philippine government “will do everything in its capacity to ensure that we are protecting our national interest.”

articles.title: PH mission to UN asserts tribunal ruling junking China’s nine-dash line claims in South China Sea
articles.description: The Philippines has quietly put forward to the United Nations an international tribunal ruling which found no basis for China’s claim to virtually the entire South China Sea but which the Duterte administration has set aside.

text.preview: Updated March 11, 2019, 11:59 p.m. MANILA, Philippines—The Philippines has quietly put forward to the United Nations an international tribunal ruling which found no basis for China’s claim to virtually the entire South China Sea but which the Duterte administration has set aside. The Philippine Permanent Mission to the UN early this month submitted its response to address China’s diplomatic note to the UN over Malaysia’s petition to extend the limits of its continental shelf in the South China Sea. “The Government of the Republic of the Philippines considers China’s positions as inconsistent with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (Unclos), which comprehensively allocates maritime rights to the States,” the Philippine Mission said in a note verbale to the UN Secretary General, Antonio Gutteres, dated March 6. “On the features in the South China Sea, the Republic of the Philippines has sovereignty and jurisdiction over the Kalayaan Island Group and Bajo de Masinloc,” it said. Malaysia filed its claim at the UN to establish its boundaries in December, angering China. “China has internal waters, territorial sea and a contiguous zone based on its Nanhai Zhudao,” the Chinese mission said in a note to the UN, referring to its islands in the South China Sea. “China has an exclusive economic zone and continental shelf…China has historic rights in the South China Sea,” it said. China claims “indisputable sovereignty” over nearly the entire South China Sea, including the West Philippine Sea. This has become clear in their aggressive actions in waters that it claims to be part of China. Manila filed a case against Beijing in the Permanent Court of Arbitration in 2012 after the China seized control of Scarborough Shoal following a standoff. articles.title: AI says China’s 9-dash line has no legal basis
articles.description: Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter).
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter). “The PRC”s nine-dash line in the South China Sea has no legal basis under international law,” said X’s AI tool Grok, referring to China by its official name’s initials. “A 2016 tribunal ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague found it invalid, as it clashes with UNCLOS” or the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The same verdict upheld the Philippines’ sovereign rights over its 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ). “China claims historic rights, but the line, drawn in 1947, overlaps with other nations’ zones, like the Philippines’ EEZ. Tensions keep rising with China’s island-building and militarization,” Grok also wrote. It noted that the nine-dash line became “ten-dash line” after Beijing added another dash east of Taiwan in 1984. It added that China’s expanded claim was “just as baseless – pure geopolitical flexing, not law.” Grok provided the information when asked by Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Commodore Jay Tarriela on his X account. Tarriela is also PCG spokesman on West Philippine Sea issues. “Hey @grok, does PRC have a legal justification of their nine-dash line or ten-dash line in the South China Sea?” asked Tarriela. The PCG official regularly provides updates on coast guard patrols aimed at stopping China’s incursions in the West Philippine Sea. The coast guard’s latest update was last March 9. articles.description: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing.

text.preview: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing. The Philippine protest, dated April 5, was posted by the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) as document No. 000228 on April 8. But the Philippine government tarried in filing the protest, doing so two years after Vietnam and Malaysia, and a year after Indonesia. Vietnam and Malaysia filed their protest a day after China submitted its 9-dash line map to the UN on May 7, 2009. Indonesia registered its protest a year ago, even if it did not have a claim on the South China Sea. The map is called “9-dash line” or “9-dotted line” because it shows a series of nine dashes or dotted lines forming a ring around the South China Sea area, which China claims is part of its territory. The area includes the Spratlys group, a cluster of oil-rich islands disputed by five other countries, including the Philippines. China has been using the map with nine dashes in asserting its territorial claim over the whole of the South Sea. But the map first made its way to the UN body, when China used it to challenge the claim made by Vietnam and Malaysia over their extended continental shelves in the South China Sea. The Vietnamese and Malaysian claims were made May 6, 2009; China filed a counter claim using the 9-dash map the next day, May 7. What followed was a series of quick exchanges where Vietnam and Malaysia responded to the Chinese protest. But it would be three months, or August 4, 2009, before the Philippines protested the submissions made by Vietnam and Malaysia. The Philippines’ April 5 2011 protest comes almost two years after its neighbors had raised the issue. (To read the 501-page Award, please go to this site : https://pca-cpa.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/175/2016/07/PH-CN-20160712-Award.pdf ) “The Tribunal found that China’s claim to historic rights to resources was incompatible with the detailed allocation of rights and maritime zones in the Convention and concluded that, to the extent China had historic rights to resources in the waters of the South China Sea, such rights were extinguished by the entry into force of the Convention to the extent they were incompatible with the Convention’s system of maritime zones,” the decision said. The Tribunal concluded that there was no legal basis for China to claim historic rights to resources, in excess of the rights provided for by the Convention, within the sea areas falling within the nine-dash line. China’s nine-dash line map covers almost 80 percent of vast South China Sea, including maritime zones of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. The Tribunal also said the presence of official personnel in high-tide features in the Spratly Islands does not change their legal status as “rocks” that do not generate an exclusive economic zone or continental shelf. China has expanded rocks it is occupying in the disputed Spratlys into artificial islands and built military structures including an airfield. The ruling also applies to the Philippines’ Pag-asa island also known as Thitu island. The Arbitral Tribunal also said China violated the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea by obstructing Philippine vessels going to Scarborough Shoal in April and May 2012 and creating a situation that endangered the ships and personnel. The Court scored China for causing harm to the coral environment by its recent large-scale land reclamation and construction of artificial islands at seven features in the Spratly Islands . articles.title: AI says China’s 9-dash line has no legal basis
articles.description: Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter).
articles.text: MANILA, Philippines — Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter). “The PRC”s nine-dash line in the South China Sea has no legal basis under international law,” said X’s AI tool Grok, referring to China by its official name’s initials. “A 2016 tribunal ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague found it invalid, as it clashes with UNCLOS” or the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The same verdict upheld the Philippines’ sovereign rights over its 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ). “China claims historic rights, but the line, drawn in 1947, overlaps with other nations’ zones, like the Philippines’ EEZ. Tensions keep rising with China’s island-building and militarization,” Grok also wrote. It noted that the nine-dash line became “ten-dash line” after Beijing added another dash east of Taiwan in 1984. It added that China’s expanded claim was “just as baseless – pure geopolitical flexing, not law.” Grok provided the information when asked by Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Commodore Jay Tarriela on his X account. Tarriela is also PCG spokesman on West Philippine Sea issues. “Hey @grok, does PRC have a legal justification of their nine-dash line or ten-dash line in the South China Sea?” asked Tarriela. The PCG official regularly provides updates on coast guard patrols aimed at stopping China’s incursions in the West Philippine Sea. The coast guard’s latest update was last March 9. text.preview: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing. The Philippine protest, dated April 5, was posted by the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) as document No. 000228 on April 8. But the Philippine government tarried in filing the protest, doing so two years after Vietnam and Malaysia, and a year after Indonesia. Vietnam and Malaysia filed their protest a day after China submitted its 9-dash line map to the UN on May 7, 2009. Indonesia registered its protest a year ago, even if it did not have a claim on the South China Sea. The map is called “9-dash line” or “9-dotted line” because it shows a series of nine dashes or dotted lines forming a ring around the South China Sea area, which China claims is part of its territory. The area includes the Spratlys group, a cluster of oil-rich islands disputed by five other countries, including the Philippines. China has been using the map with nine dashes in asserting its territorial claim over the whole of the South Sea. But the map first made its way to the UN body, when China used it to challenge the claim made by Vietnam and Malaysia over their extended continental shelves in the South China Sea. The Vietnamese and Malaysian claims were made May 6, 2009; China filed a counter claim using the 9-dash map the next day, May 7. What followed was a series of quick exchanges where Vietnam and Malaysia responded to the Chinese protest. But it would be three months, or August 4, 2009, before the Philippines protested the submissions made by Vietnam and Malaysia. The Philippines’ April 5 2011 protest comes almost two years after its neighbors had raised the issue. text.preview: The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled today that China’s all-encompassing nine-dash line is not valid . (To read the 501-page Award, please go to this site : https://pca-cpa.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/175/2016/07/PH-CN-20160712-Award.pdf ) “The Tribunal found that China’s claim to historic rights to resources was incompatible with the detailed allocation of rights and maritime zones in the Convention and concluded that, to the extent China had historic rights to resources in the waters of the South China Sea, such rights were extinguished by the entry into force of the Convention to the extent they were incompatible with the Convention’s system of maritime zones,” the decision said. The Tribunal concluded that there was no legal basis for China to claim historic rights to resources, in excess of the rights provided for by the Convention, within the sea areas falling within the nine-dash line. China’s nine-dash line map covers almost 80 percent of vast South China Sea, including maritime zones of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. The Tribunal also said the presence of official personnel in high-tide features in the Spratly Islands does not change their legal status as “rocks” that do not generate an exclusive economic zone or continental shelf. China has expanded rocks it is occupying in the disputed Spratlys into artificial islands and built military structures including an airfield. The ruling also applies to the Philippines’ Pag-asa island also known as Thitu island. The Arbitral Tribunal also said China violated the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea by obstructing Philippine vessels going to Scarborough Shoal in April and May 2012 and creating a situation that endangered the ships and personnel. The Court scored China for causing harm to the coral environment by its recent large-scale land reclamation and construction of artificial islands at seven features in the Spratly Islands . Marcos said that when he took office, his duty was to defend the country's territory.

In a statement, the Department of Foreign Affairs said the 2023 edition map is China's latest attempt "to legitimize purported sovereignty and jurisdiction over Philippine features and maritime zones has no basis under international law, particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)."

"The 2016 Arbitral Award invalidated the nine-dashed line. The Philippine government has adopted the name West Philippine Sea to refer to parts of the South China Sea within its territory that are also being claimed by China.

China, the DFA said, should "act responsibly and abide by its obligations under UNCLOS and the final and binding 2016 Arbitral Award."

“We do not even recognize the nine-dash line, much more the 10-dash line,” National Security Adviser Eduardo Año said during the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) press conference on Thursday.

“The arbitral award is final and binding and it gives us our maritime entitlement, our extended economic zone, our territorial waters, and even our extended continental shelf,” he added.

article.title: PH protests China's 9-dash line claim over Spratlys
article.description: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing.

text.preview: THE Philippines has lodged a diplomatic protest against China’s 9-dash line territorial claim over the whole of South China Sea, a month before President Aquino’s planned state visit to Beijing. The Philippine protest, dated April 5, was posted by the United Nations Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf (CLCS) as document No. 000228 on April 8. But the Philippine government tarried in filing the protest, doing so two years after Vietnam and Malaysia, and a year after Indonesia. Vietnam and Malaysia filed their protest a day after China submitted its 9-dash line map to the UN on May 7, 2009. Indonesia registered its protest a year ago, even if it did not have a claim on the South China Sea. The map is called “9-dash line” or “9-dotted line” because it shows a series of nine dashes or dotted lines forming a ring around the South China Sea area, which China claims is part of its territory. The area includes the Spratlys group, a cluster of oil-rich islands disputed by five other countries, including the Philippines. China has been using the map with nine dashes in asserting its territorial claim over the whole of the South Sea. But the map first made its way to the UN body, when China used it to challenge the claim made by Vietnam and Malaysia over their extended continental shelves in the South China Sea. The Vietnamese and Malaysian claims were made May 6, 2009; China filed a counter claim using the 9-dash map the next day, May 7. What followed was a series of quick exchanges where Vietnam and Malaysia responded to the Chinese protest. But it would be three months, or August 4, 2009, before the Philippines protested the submissions made by Vietnam and Malaysia. The Philippines’ April 5 2011 protest comes almost two years after its neighbors had raised the issue. text.preview: The Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled today that China’s all-encompassing nine-dash line is not valid . (To read the 501-page Award, please go to this site : https://pca-cpa.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/175/2016/07/PH-CN-20160712-Award.pdf ) “The Tribunal found that China’s claim to historic rights to resources was incompatible with the detailed allocation of rights and maritime zones in the Convention and concluded that, to the extent China had historic rights to resources in the waters of the South China Sea, such rights were extinguished by the entry into force of the Convention to the extent they were incompatible with the Convention’s system of maritime zones,” the decision said. The Tribunal concluded that there was no legal basis for China to claim historic rights to resources, in excess of the rights provided for by the Convention, within the sea areas falling within the nine-dash line. China’s nine-dash line map covers almost 80 percent of vast South China Sea, including maritime zones of the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan. The Tribunal also said the presence of official personnel in high-tide features in the Spratly Islands does not change their legal status as “rocks” that do not generate an exclusive economic zone or continental shelf. China has expanded rocks it is occupying in the disputed Spratlys into artificial islands and built military structures including an airfield. The ruling also applies to the Philippines’ Pag-asa island also known as Thitu island. The Arbitral Tribunal also said China violated the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea by obstructing Philippine vessels going to Scarborough Shoal in April and May 2012 and creating a situation that endangered the ships and personnel. The Court scored China for causing harm to the coral environment by its recent large-scale land reclamation and construction of artificial islands at seven features in the Spratly Islands . article.title: Philippines rejects new Chinese ‘10-dash line’ map
article.description: The Philippines on Thursday rejected China's publication of a new map that places nearly the entire South China Sea within its national boundaries, infringing on Manila's claims in the resource-rich waters.

text.preview:
The Philippines on Thursday rejected China's publication of a new map that places nearly the entire South China Sea within its national boundaries, infringing on Manila's claims in the resource-rich waters.

In a statement, the Department of Foreign Affairs said the 2023 edition map is China's latest attempt "to legitimize purported sovereignty and jurisdiction over Philippine features and maritime zones has no basis under international law, particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)."

"The 2016 Arbitral Award invalidated the nine-dashed line. It categorically stated that 'maritime areas of the South China Sea encompassed by the relevant part of the ‘nine-dash line’ are contrary to the Convention and without lawful effect to the extent that they exceed the geographic and substantive limits of China’s maritime entitlements under the Convention,'" the DFA said.

The Philippine government has adopted the name West Philippine Sea to refer to parts of the South China Sea within its territory that are also being claimed by China.

China, the DFA said, should "act responsibly and abide by its obligations under UNCLOS and the final and binding 2016 Arbitral Award."

“We do not even recognize the nine-dash line, much more the 10-dash line,” National Security Adviser Eduardo Año said during the National Task Force to End Local Communist Armed Conflict (NTF-ELCAC) press conference on Thursday.

“The arbitral award is final and binding and it gives us our maritime entitlement, our extended economic zone, our territorial waters, and even our extended continental shelf,” he added.

He said that the Philippine government “will do everything in its capacity to ensure that we are protecting our national interest.”

China claims “indisputable sovereignty” over nearly the entire South China Sea, including the West Philippine Sea. article.title: AI says China’s 9-dash line has no legal basis
article.description: Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter).
article.text: MANILA, Philippines — Even artificial intelligence (AI) acknowledges that the so-called nine-dash-line claim of China in the South China Sea is “invalid,” according to an AI tool created by X (formerly Twitter). “The PRC”s nine-dash line in the South China Sea has no legal basis under international law,” said X’s AI tool Grok, referring to China by its official name’s initials. “A 2016 tribunal ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague found it invalid, as it clashes with UNCLOS” or the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. The same verdict upheld the Philippines’ sovereign rights over its 200-nautical mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ). “China claims historic rights, but the line, drawn in 1947, overlaps with other nations’ zones, like the Philippines’ EEZ. Tensions keep rising with China’s island-building and militarization,” Grok also wrote. It noted that the nine-dash line became “ten-dash line” after Beijing added another dash east of Taiwan in 1984. It added that China’s expanded claim was “just as baseless – pure geopolitical flexing, not law.” Grok provided the information when asked by Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) Commodore Jay Tarriela on his X account. Tarriela is also PCG spokesman on West Philippine Sea issues. “Hey @grok, does PRC have a legal justification of their nine-dash line or ten-dash line in the South China Sea?” asked Tarriela. The PCG official regularly provides updates on coast guard patrols aimed at stopping China’s incursions in the West Philippine Sea. The coast guard’s latest update was last March 9. input.text: 'NAKARATING NA PO BA KAYO NG BARMM?' Senator-judge Robinhood Padilla asked former state auditor Roderick Wamil if he had ever visited the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) and whether he was aware of the country's ongoing terrorism threats. During his interjection, Padilla raised preliminary questions about the Audit Observation Memorandum, trying to establish ties to the confidential funds used by Vice President Sara Duterte for surveillance on potential New People's Army (NPA) recruitment. "Pero kayo po ang humahawak ng imbestigasyon patungkol sa confidential funds, tama po ba?" Padilla asked Wamil. "Hindi po siya imbestigasyon. Evaluation po," the witness answered. "Kayo po ba ay naniniwala na ang mga confidential agent ay dapat magpakilala? Sabihin ang kanilang totoong pangalan," the senator furthered. "Wala pong provisions as to that po sa joint circular," Wamil said. Padilla then asked Wamil to define "confidential," to which the auditor replied, "classified."

Sa kanyang naging post nitong Huwebes, August 6, inamin niyang hindi siya nakatiis kaya naghayag siya ng saloobin tungkol sa pahayag ng senador. Umpisa ni Mendoza, “Pasensya ka na sa isang irrelevant, talunan at matandang kahit retired na ay nagsisikap pa ring makapag-bayad ng tax para may pampasweldo sa inyo! Nung auditor po ako, naka akyat ako ng mga bundok. Rebel Returnees’ Fund po kasi ang inaudit namin nuon. Hindi lang po bundok, tumawid ng ilog, may pandong na sako.” Baka Bet Mo: Heidi Mendoza sa LGBTQIA rights: Kailan naging katatawanan ang pagkatao ng iba? Pagpapatuloy ni Mendoza, naranasan na rin niyang magbilang ng coconut trees at ang mapaulanan ng bala ng baril ang kaniyang kasamahan sa Lanao. “Napunta na rin po kami ng BARMM, may kasamahan kaming pinaulanan ng bala habang nasa Lanao. Naranasang akyatin ang tinutuluyang staff house, etc. Ganyan po ka exciting ang buhay auditor,” lahad ng dating komisyuner. Ayon pa kay Mendoza, hindi raw drama na maituturing kung marami raw ang mga auditors na nagretiro dahil sa hirap ng kanilang trabaho. “Pero, depende po sa audit na isinasagawa. Ang hindi lang namin nagawa, mag-taping hanggang umagahin. Real po kasi ang audit hindi reels. Hindi po acting lang kung kami ay takutin! “Kung mamalasin ay kukulangin pa sa pambili ng gamot kapag nagkaroon ng malubhang karamdaman bunga ng stress sa trabaho at stress na rin tuwing may hearing, impeachment man o simpleng budget hearing. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. text.preview:

The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

output.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
output.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

articles.title: OVP secret funds may have helped stop rebel attacks – Padilla
articles.description: Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the OVP confidential fund releases may have helped prevent rebel attacks.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential fund releases to the founding anniversaries of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) and the National Democratic Front (NDF), suggesting the funds may have helped prevent rebel attacks. On the 13th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Padilla questioned prosecution witness Roderick Wamil about three P125 million confidential fund checks issued in late 2022 and early 2023. Wamil is the former state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) who audited the P500 million confidential funds released to the OVP in four 125 million increments, as well as the P112.5 million for the Department of Education (DepEd) released in three checks worth 37.5 million each. “Itong pong mga dates na ito, nung December 26, March 29, April 24, lahat po ito walang nangyaring attack. Lahat po foiled. Wala po. For the first time, wala pong nangyaring attack. Kasi tuwing founding anniversary, may attack,” Padilla said. “On all of these dates, December 26, March 29, April 24, there were no attacks. Every single one was foiled. There’s none. For the first time, there were no attacks because every time the CPP-NPA celebrates its founding anniversary, there is usually an attack.” Padilla said in Filipino. When he started his clarificatory questions to the witness, Padilla referred to the first check for the OVP and asked, “Yung una pong cheke ay 125 million, December 20, 2022. articles.description: SINAGOT ng former COA commissioner Heidi Mendoza ang sinabi ni Sen. Robin Padilla patungkol sa pag-akyat ng mga COA auditors sa bundok.

Sa kanyang naging post nitong Huwebes, August 6, inamin niyang hindi siya nakatiis kaya naghayag siya ng saloobin tungkol sa pahayag ng senador. Umpisa ni Mendoza, “Pasensya ka na sa isang irrelevant, talunan at matandang kahit retired na ay nagsisikap pa ring makapag-bayad ng tax para may pampasweldo sa inyo! Nung auditor po ako, naka akyat ako ng mga bundok. Rebel Returnees’ Fund po kasi ang inaudit namin nuon. Hindi lang po bundok, tumawid ng ilog, may pandong na sako.” Baka Bet Mo: Heidi Mendoza sa LGBTQIA rights: Kailan naging katatawanan ang pagkatao ng iba? articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. articles.title: DOJ prosecutors seek raps vs Basilan mayor over 2025 poll attack
articles.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. Public officials entrusted with confidential funds must account for how public money was spent,” she said in an online press briefing on Thursday. Wamil’s testimony unquestionably advanced the prosecution’s case. articles.description: Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica, as the two people with the clearest knowledge of how the funds were handled and spent. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential fund releases to the founding anniversaries of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) and the National Democratic Front (NDF), suggesting the funds may have helped prevent rebel attacks. On the 13th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Padilla questioned prosecution witness Roderick Wamil about three P125 million confidential fund checks issued in late 2022 and early 2023. articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. articles.title: DOJ prosecutors seek raps vs Basilan mayor over 2025 poll attack
articles.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. Public officials entrusted with confidential funds must account for how public money was spent,” she said in an online press briefing on Thursday. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica, as the two people with the clearest knowledge of how the funds were handled and spent. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. articles.title: VP Duterte staff asked COA to issue audit query instead of observation memo—witness | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff a

text.preview: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education . Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

articles.description: Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Counter-insurgency programs (P9.375 million in Q1; P9.3 million in Q2; P9.2 million in Q3)
  • Abuse prevention and control within schools (P10 million in Q1; P10.075 million in Q2; P10.125 million in Q3)
  • Anti-illegal activities operations (P9 million in Q1; P9.1 million in Q2; P9.14 million in Q3)
  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. Public officials entrusted with confidential funds must account for how public money was spent,” she said in an online press briefing on Thursday. Wamil’s testimony unquestionably advanced the prosecution’s case. articles.description: Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

articles.description: Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Counter-insurgency programs (P9.375 million in Q1; P9.3 million in Q2; P9.2 million in Q3)

  • Anti-illegal activities operations (P9 million in Q1; P9.1 million in Q2; P9.14 million in Q3)
  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)
