article.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
article.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. article.title: VP Duterte staff asked COA to issue audit query instead of observation memo—witness | ABS-CBN News
article.description: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff a

text.preview: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education . Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. article.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
article.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

article.description: Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

article.title: OVP secret funds may have helped stop rebel attacks – Padilla
article.description: Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the OVP confidential fund releases may have helped prevent rebel attacks.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential fund releases to the founding anniversaries of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) and the National Democratic Front (NDF), suggesting the funds may have helped prevent rebel attacks. On the 13th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Padilla questioned prosecution witness Roderick Wamil about three P125 million confidential fund checks issued in late 2022 and early 2023. Wamil is the former state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) who audited the P500 million confidential funds released to the OVP in four 125 million increments, as well as the P112.5 million for the Department of Education (DepEd) released in three checks worth 37.5 million each. “Itong pong mga dates na ito, nung December 26, March 29, April 24, lahat po ito walang nangyaring attack. Lahat po foiled. Wala po. For the first time, wala pong nangyaring attack. Kasi tuwing founding anniversary, may attack,” Padilla said. “On all of these dates, December 26, March 29, April 24, there were no attacks. Every single one was foiled. There’s none. For the first time, there were no attacks because every time the CPP-NPA celebrates its founding anniversary, there is usually an attack.” Padilla said in Filipino. When he started his clarificatory questions to the witness, Padilla referred to the first check for the OVP and asked, “Yung una pong cheke ay 125 million, December 20, 2022. article.title: Heidi Mendoza kay Robin Padilla: May pondo para sugpuin korapsyon!
article.description: SINAGOT ng former COA commissioner Heidi Mendoza ang sinabi ni Sen. Robin Padilla patungkol sa pag-akyat ng mga COA auditors sa bundok.

text.preview: SINAGOT ng former commissioner ng Commission on Audit (COA) na si Heidi Mendoza ang sinabi ni Sen. Robin Padilla patungkol sa pag-akyat ng mga COA auditors sa bundok. Sa kanyang naging post nitong Huwebes, August 6, inamin niyang hindi siya nakatiis kaya naghayag siya ng saloobin tungkol sa pahayag ng senador. Umpisa ni Mendoza, “Pasensya ka na sa isang irrelevant, talunan at matandang kahit retired na ay nagsisikap pa ring makapag-bayad ng tax para may pampasweldo sa inyo! Nung auditor po ako, naka akyat ako ng mga bundok. Rebel Returnees’ Fund po kasi ang inaudit namin nuon. Hindi lang po bundok, tumawid ng ilog, may pandong na sako.” Baka Bet Mo: Heidi Mendoza sa LGBTQIA rights: Kailan naging katatawanan ang pagkatao ng iba? Pagpapatuloy ni Mendoza, naranasan na rin niyang magbilang ng coconut trees at ang mapaulanan ng bala ng baril ang kaniyang kasamahan sa Lanao. “Napunta na rin po kami ng BARMM, may kasamahan kaming pinaulanan ng bala habang nasa Lanao. Naranasang akyatin ang tinutuluyang staff house, etc. Ganyan po ka exciting ang buhay auditor,” lahad ng dating komisyuner. Ayon pa kay Mendoza, hindi raw drama na maituturing kung marami raw ang mga auditors na nagretiro dahil sa hirap ng kanilang trabaho. “Pero, depende po sa audit na isinasagawa. Ang hindi lang namin nagawa, mag-taping hanggang umagahin. Real po kasi ang audit hindi reels. Hindi po acting lang kung kami ay takutin! “Kung mamalasin ay kukulangin pa sa pambili ng gamot kapag nagkaroon ng malubhang karamdaman bunga ng stress sa trabaho at stress na rin tuwing may hearing, impeachment man o simpleng budget hearing. Lalo na kung court hearing,” sabi pa ni Mendoza. article.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
article.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. article.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

article.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
article.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. Public officials entrusted with confidential funds must account for how public money was spent,” she said in an online press briefing on Thursday. article.description: Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica, as the two people with the clearest knowledge of how the funds were handled and spent.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica, as the two people with the clearest knowledge of how the funds were handled and spent. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. article.title: VP Duterte staff asked COA to issue audit query instead of observation memo—witness | ABS-CBN News
article.description: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff a

text.preview: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education . Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. article.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

On the 13th day of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial, Padilla questioned prosecution witness Roderick Wamil about three P125 million confidential fund checks issued in late 2022 and early 2023. Wamil is the former state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) who audited the P500 million confidential funds released to the OVP in four 125 million increments, as well as the P112.5 million for the Department of Education (DepEd) released in three checks worth 37.5 million each. “Itong pong mga dates na ito, nung December 26, March 29, April 24, lahat po ito walang nangyaring attack. Lahat po foiled. Wala po. For the first time, wala pong nangyaring attack. Kasi tuwing founding anniversary, may attack,” Padilla said. “On all of these dates, December 26, March 29, April 24, there were no attacks. Every single one was foiled. There’s none. article.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
article.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. article.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. The eighth week of Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment trial ended with the Senate impeachment court focusing on a basic question: Who knew where the P500 million confidential funds went? Over three days —the 17th, 18th and 19th days of the trial — the testimony from two ranking officials of the Office of the Vice President pointed to Duterte and her former security chief, Col. Raymund Dante Lachica, as the two people with the clearest knowledge of how the funds were handled and spent. Assistant Secretary Lemuel Ortonio, the OVP assistant chief of staff, gave the most important testimony of the week. He told the court that Duterte knew about and authorized the activities involving confidential funds under her office. Asked by Presiding Officer Francis Escudero whether Duterte knew, supervised and authorized the entire process, from requesting the funds and withdrawing them to their release, spending, liquidation and responses to the Commission on Audit, Ortonio answered: “Yes, Your Honor.” His testimony followed two days of questioning of Gina Acosta, Duterte’s former special disbursing officer, now a staff officer VI at the OVP. A system of trust, or a break in accountability? Acosta said she released P125 million in cash to Lachica on Duterte’s instructions in December 2022. The money was the first tranche of the P500 million in OVP confidential funds now under scrutiny, disbursed from December 2022 to September 2023. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. articles.title: VP Duterte staff asked COA to issue audit query instead of observation memo—witness | ABS-CBN News
articles.description: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff a

text.preview: COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education . Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News/File MANILA — Officials under Vice President Sara Duterte once asked the Commission on Audit's Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Unit (COA-ICFAU) to issue an "audit query" instead of an Audit Observation Memorandum (AOM), an auditor who testified as a witness in Duterte's impeachment trial said Tuesday. Witness flags 'violations' in OVP confidential fund use COA auditor Roderick Wamil, who previously served with the ICFAU, said the request was made during a September 2023 meeting with Zuleika Lopez, chief of staff at the Office of the Vice President, and Michael Poa, former spokesperson for the Department of Education. Duterte had previously served as Education secretary. "They asked about the liquidation process ng cash advances [for confidential funds], as well as kung ano 'yong mga supporting documents required," Wamil said, recalling the meeting that also involved former ICFAU head Nilda Plaras. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. When asked about the response of the two, Wamil continued: "They asked if instead of Audit Observation Memorandum in case may audit findings, audit query na lang po 'yong i-issue sa kanila." Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. The ICFAU did not agree to issue audit queries and instead continued issuing AOMs when it found audit findings, Wamil added. articles.title: EXPLAINER: What is 'evidence of success' in the use of confidential funds?
articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

During direct examination, Wamil testified that the OVP reported spending P42 million in confidential funds for the provision of medical and food aid from February 6 to March 29, 2023, and another P40 million for the same purpose from April 25 to June 30, 2023, for a total of P82 million.

"Our findings, or observations, were that the OVP did not submit documentary evidence of payments for the first and second quarters of 2023," Wamil said in response to questions from House prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan.

"Second, based on its accomplishment report, it indicated that rewards had been paid, but the OVP did not submit any document evidencing the success of the information-gathering or surveillance activities resulting from the information provided by the informant, in violation of the joint circular," he added.

Under COA Joint Circular No. 2015-01, which sets the guidelines on the use of confidential and intelligence funds, CF is allocated to agencies for Confidential Expenses, or expenses for “surveillance activities in civilian government agencies that are intended to support the mandate or operations of the agency.”

articles.description: Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

text.preview:
Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

Prosecution

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

According to Wamil, the unsupported disbursements included purchases of medicines and food assistance, as well as the payment of rewards and incentives for travel related to confidential operations, whose authenticity could not be verified due to the absence of the required documentation.

Wamil also testified that the Department of Education failed to submit supporting documents for the disbursement of P112.5 million in confidential funds in 2023, which were reportedly used for the following:

  • Counter-insurgency programs (P9.375 million in Q1; P9.3 million in Q2; P9.2 million in Q3)
  • Abuse prevention and control within schools (P10 million in Q1; P10.075 million in Q2; P10.125 million in Q3)
  • Anti-illegal activities operations (P9 million in Q1; P9.1 million in Q2; P9.14 million in Q3)
  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

articles.description: Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the OVP confidential fund releases may have helped prevent rebel attacks.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — Senator Robinhood Padilla on Wednesday linked the timing of the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) confidential fund releases to the founding anniversaries of the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People’s Army (CPP-NPA) and the National Democratic Front (NDF), suggesting the funds may have helped prevent rebel attacks. Wamil is the former state auditor of the Commission on Audit-Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO) who audited the P500 million confidential funds released to the OVP in four 125 million increments, as well as the P112.5 million for the Department of Education (DepEd) released in three checks worth 37.5 million each. “Itong pong mga dates na ito, nung December 26, March 29, April 24, lahat po ito walang nangyaring attack. Lahat po foiled. Wala po. For the first time, wala pong nangyaring attack. Kasi tuwing founding anniversary, may attack,” Padilla said. “On all of these dates, December 26, March 29, April 24, there were no attacks. Every single one was foiled. There’s none. articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. articles.title: DOJ prosecutors seek raps vs Basilan mayor over 2025 poll attack
articles.description: State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day.

text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. Regional police officials said the case that the BARMM regional prosecutors have recommended for filing in court against the respondents is related to the offshore attack before dawn on May 12 last year in the sea close to the beachfront Barangay Sangbay Big in Hadji Muhtamad by gunmen riding speedboats, allegedly owned by the mayor, of supporters and poll watchers of then mayoral candidate Hadji Jamar Abdullah Mansul. articles.description: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

text.preview:
The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte has entered its second month, with the Senate impeachment court now delving into the technical details surrounding the alleged misuse of confidential funds under Article I.

One of the key terms that surfaced during the proceedings is "evidence of success."

What does "evidence of success" mean?

The term came up during the prosecution's questioning of state auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly of the Commission on Audit Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), the office that audited confidential and intelligence funds lodged with various government offices, including the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) under Duterte.

Lawyer Roderick Wamil, a former state auditor with the Commission on Audit’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office (COA-ICFAO), returned to the witness stand on Tuesday to testify on the disbursement of more than P200 million in confidential funds of the Office of the Vice President (OVP) and the Department of Education (DepEd) during Vice President Sara Duterte’s tenure as education secretary.

During the prosecution's presentation of evidence, Wamil testified that at least P129 million of the OVP's P250-million confidential fund allocation for the first and second quarters of 2023 lacked supporting documents proving that the disbursements were made for their intended purposes, in violation of Joint Circular No. 2015-01 governing the use of confidential and intelligence funds.

  • Anti-extremism/terrorism programs (P9.125 million in Q1; P9.025 million in Q2; P9.035 million in Q3)

articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. articles.title: Palace: Reinforce security ahead of BARMM election
articles.description: The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The government is set to reinforce security in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao as the first-ever BARMM parliamentary election approaches, Malacañang said yesterday. Palace press officer Claire Castro said President Marcos has directed concerned agencies to ensure a peaceful, orderly and credible conduct of the BARMM polls on Sept. 14. Castro clarified that the reported killings in BARMM since the start of the year were not related to the upcoming polls, and instead involved personal conflicts, citing information from the Commission on Elections. She said the Comelec, Philippine National Police (PNP) and Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) are conducting focused law enforcement operations against private armed groups and other security threats in the region. Marcos earlier assured the Bangsamoro people that the first parliamentary election would push through as scheduled. Castro said 8,299 PNP personnel would be deployed in BARMM for election security. She added that the number may be augmented as the election approaches, depending on the PNP’s threat assessment and the Comelec requirements. “The PNP is working alongside the AFP and the Philippine Coast Guard to boost security, particularly in election areas of concern identified by the Comelec, to ensure the safe, peaceful and orderly conduct of the election,” Castro said. Meanwhile, 12 people have been arrested for violating the Comelec gun ban, as security operations intensify. PNP chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez said the arrests came as police continue implementing security measures during the campaign period, noting that no violent election-related incident has been reported so far. “We have already laid out and are implementing our security operations,” Nartatez said. text.preview: COTABATO CITY, Philippines — State prosecutors in the Bangsamoro region had recommended the filing of criminal cases against a mayor in Basilan and several others for their alleged involvement in a deadly election-related gun attack hours before the May 12, 2025 polling day. Radio reports on Friday, August 7, stated that the resolution of the Regional Prosecution Office 14 mentioned Arsina Kahing Nanoh, mayor of Hadji Muhtamad, her husband Nadz Nanoh, and relatives Walihiul Allama, Hadji Rahim Kahim, Lucman Kahim, Tudy Bayro, Sing Hassan and several others, tagged only as “john does,” as respondents to the three counts of murder, two counts of frustrated murder and attempted murder that prosecutors are to file in a court. The RPO 14 of the Department of Justice covers the five provinces in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, Maguindanao del Sur, Maguindanao del Norte, Lanao del Sur, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi, and the cities of Lamitan, Marawi and Cotabato, where the BARMM regional capitol is located. Copies of the RPO 14's resolution pertaining to its case buildup against Nano, one of the 11 municipal mayors in Basilan, and several others, were obtained on Wednesday by reporters from officials of the Police Regional Office-Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Camp SK Pendatun in Parang, Maguindanao del Norte and the military’s Western Mindanao Command based in Zamboanga City. The resolution, dated July 2, 2026, was signed by four officials of RPO 14. articles.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
articles.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

text.preview: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. The proceedings from Days 11 to 13 demonstrate why impeachment trials should never be judged by dramatic courtroom exchanges alone. Beneath the debate over acknowledgment receipts, unusual names and missing documents lies a more consequential question: Has the prosecution shown that Duterte committed an impeachable offense, or has it primarily revealed deficiencies in the government’s auditing framework? Lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro repeatedly says the prosecution’s case does not hinge on whether the names were aliases or genuine persons. “The important issue is accountability. Public officials entrusted with confidential funds must account for how public money was spent,” she said in an online press briefing on Thursday. But Acosta admitted that she did not personally know how Lachica spent the money. She said she relied on the documents he gave her when she prepared the liquidation reports. Plaras had referred the officials to a joint circular that detailed the authorized use of confidential and intelligence funds. "Sinabi rin po ni Assistant Commissioner Nilda Plaras na in case may makitang findings during the audit ay magi-issue ng AOM," Wamil said. Wamil said he was not familiar what an audit query was since it was not among the issuances under the joint circular. article.title: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial, Week 5: Beyond the receipts
article.description: Five weeks into the trial, the proceedings have become about more than the fate of one elected official. They have evolved into an examination of how the Philippine government accounts for billions of pesos in confidential funds and whether the existing safeguards are sufficient to protect public money from misuse.

She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Three days of testimony from Commission on Audit auditor Roderick Wamil, formerly assigned to the agency’s Intelligence and Confidential Funds Audit Office, has shifted the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte from a largely political spectacle into a searching examination of confidential fund safeguards. In the process, the Senate impeachment court has exposed not only the strengths and weaknesses of the prosecution’s case but also the institutional gaps that have long surrounded the auditing of secret government expenditures. input.text: His work helped defend the Philippines. American marine biologist Dr. Kent Carpenter, whose scientific testimony supported the Philippines in its landmark 2016 South China Sea arbitration case against China, was shot and killed during a home invasion in Negros Oriental province in the Central Visayas region of the Philippines. Police said three unidentified men forcibly entered Carpenter's home in Barangay Ajong, Sibulan, on the night of July 12. One of the intruders allegedly shot the 73-year-old scientist in the head, killing him. His 34-year-old companion was also injured. The suspects remain at large, and investigators are reviewing CCTV footage, interviewing witnesses, and pursuing leads. Police Brigadier General Romano Cardiño condemned the killing as a "senseless act of violence" and vowed to bring those responsible to justice. Carpenter was widely respected in the scientific community for his decades of work in the Philippines. He first began studying the country's marine ecosystems in 1975 and became one of the world's leading experts on Philippine marine biodiversity. Beyond his scientific achievements, Carpenter also played a significant role in one of the Philippines' biggest international legal victories. During the South China Sea arbitration initiated by the Philippines in 2013, he submitted expert written evidence documenting the environmental damage caused by China's island reclamation and destructive fishing practices in the West Philippine Sea. He also delivered oral testimony during the 2015 merits hearing. The tribunal's 2016 ruling overwhelmingly favored the Philippines and found no legal basis for China's sweeping "nine-dash line" claims. Carpenter also conducted extensive research in the Verde Island Passage, often called the "center of the center" of global marine shore fish biodiversity, and was a strong advocate for having the area recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. His death has prompted tributes from Silliman University, the University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute, conservation groups, and fellow scientists. Many remembered him not only as a world-class researcher, but also as a generous mentor who spent five decades helping Filipinos better understand and protect their country's extraordinary marine ecosystems. His life reminds us that science can shape history just as much as politics or diplomacy—and that the people behind those contributions are often remembered long after the headlines fade.

content_profile.verification_text:
American marine biologist Dr. Kent Carpenter, whose scientific testimony supported the Philippines in its landmark 2016 South China Sea arbitration case against China, was shot and killed during a home invasion in Negros Oriental province in the Central Visayas region of the Philippines.
Police said three unidentified men forcibly entered Carpenter's home in Barangay Ajong, Sibulan, on the night of July 12.
His 34-year-old companion was also injured.
The suspects remain at large, and investigators are reviewing CCTV footage, interviewing witnesses, and pursuing leads.
Police Brigadier General Romano Cardiño condemned the killing as a "senseless act of violence" and vowed to bring those responsible to justice.
He first began studying the country's marine ecosystems in 1975 and became one of the world's leading experts on Philippine marine biodiversity.
During the South China Sea arbitration initiated by the Philippines in 2013, he submitted expert written evidence documenting the environmental damage caused by China's island reclamation and destructive fishing practices in the West Philippine Sea.
He also delivered oral testimony during the 2015 merits hearing.
The tribunal's 2016 ruling overwhelmingly favored the Philippines and found no legal basis for China's sweeping "nine-dash line" claims.
Carpenter also conducted extensive research in the Verde Island Passage, often called the "center of the center" of global marine shore fish biodiversity, and was a strong advocate for having the area recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
His death has prompted tributes from Silliman University, the University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute, conservation groups, and fellow scientists.

In a statement, Advocates of Science and Technology for the People (Agham) described Carpenter as “a scientist and advocate” whose decades of work in studying and protecting Philippine marine ecosystems reflected his commitment to making science serve the people. The organization noted that Carpenter was a leading advocate for the protection of the Verde Island Passage, which his research identified as the world’s “center of the center of marine shorefish biodiversity.” It also cited his support for protecting the marine corridor under the Expanded National Integrated Protected Areas System and efforts to have it declared a United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (Unesco) World Heritage Site. output.description: The live-in partner of American marine biologist Kent Carpenter and her sibling are considered persons of interest in his recent killing.

text.preview: BIODIVERSITY DEFENDER A composite image of Dr. Kent Carpenter and the Verde Island Passage from Sentro para sa Ikauunlad ng Katutubong Aghamat Teknolohiya, California Academy of Sciences, and University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute BIODIVERSITY DEFENDER A composite image of Dr. Kent Carpenter and the Verde Island Passage from Sentro para sa Ikauunlad ng Katutubong Aghamat Teknolohiya, California Academy of Sciences, and University of the Philippines Marine Science Institute MANILA, Philippines — The live-in partner of American marine biologist Kent Carpenter and her sibling are considered persons of interest in his recent killing in Sibulan, Negros Oriental, the police said on Wednesday. Carpenter, 73, and his 34-year-old Filipino female companion were having dinner at home Sunday night when three men in balaclavas barged in, one of them shooting the biologist in the head and killing him instantly, according to the initial investigation. “We can’t say she (live-in partner) is involved. But for now, since she was left alive, the suspects may know her,” Negros Oriental police chief Col. Timmar Alam told reporters in a phone interview. “As for the live-in partner’s sibling, the sibling is one of those who frequently visited the house,” he added. READ: Scientists seek justice for slain American marine biologist The police withheld identity of the victim’s live-in partner, who was earlier reported to have sustained minor injuries, and that of her sibling pending the findings of a task force created for the case. Carpenter’s killing came as a shock to his peers in the scientific and academic circles particularly at Silliman University in Dumaguete City, where he was an adjunct professor at the Institute of Environmental and Marine Sciences and worked alongside the late National Scientist and Ramon Magsaysay Awardee Dr. Angel Alcala.
