articles.description: The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.
articles.text:
The Philippine National Police is looking into the possibility that the violent behavior of one of the two minor suspects in Monday's fatal shooting at San Jose National High School in Tacloban City may have been influenced by the online game GoreBox.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Tuesday, Police Brig. Gen. Jayson Capoy, director of the Police Regional Office in Eastern Visayas, said the 14-year-old suspect had been playing GoreBox, a sandbox-style game that allows players to create and destroy objects and simulate chaos using various weapons.

Investigators are also looking into reports that the attack may have been rooted in bullying, based on the suspects’ initial statements.

Capoy clarified that the death toll remained at three, while 20 others were injured. Of the injured, 15 sustained gunshot wounds, while the rest were hurt while trying to escape, police said.

The two suspects, aged 14 and 15, both Grade 9 students and reportedly close friends, allegedly entered two classrooms and opened fire on their schoolmates before they were arrested.

Police recovered a Glock pistol and a .38-caliber revolver from the scene. One of the firearms was reportedly issued to a police officer relative, who is now under investigation.

The Department of Education has since coordinated with local authorities and social welfare agencies to provide medical and psychosocial support to affected students and school personnel.

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has ordered a full investigation and heightened security measures in schools and other public areas.—MCG GMA News

articles.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. text.preview: MANILA — The government's temporary ban on the video game GoreBox following the deadly Tacloban school shooting has triggered a wider debate over whether video games are being unfairly blamed for a much deeper problem. The Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (CICC) temporarily blocked access to GoreBox after investigators found that one of the teenage suspects regularly played the game. The June 22 shooting at San Jose National High School left three students dead and 20 others injured, one of the deadliest school shootings in recent Philippine history. "Walang study na nagpapatunay na yung games nakaka-effect sa real life behavior ng gamer. Pero mayroong study nagpapatunay na walang effect ito sa real life behavior nung naglalaro." text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. articles.title: Tacloban shooting may be first 'completed' attack by 764 extremist network — expert
articles.description: The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The Tacloban school shooting may be the first mass shooting the online extremist network 764 carried out to completion anywhere in the world, a cybersecurity expert told senators on Wednesday, July 1. Angel Redoble, chair of the Philippine Institute of Cyber Security Professionals, shared his assessment at the Senate panel's first hearing on the June 22 attack at San Jose National High School in Tacloban. The same hearing also saw the Philippine National Police (PNP) disclose that it has rescued at least 24 minors part of the same broad online network since October 2025. Five of the children rescued were found to have harmed themselves. "The first completed mass shooting, if we can finally attribute that to 764, that will be the first," Redoble said. "Because in 2025 [in the United States], it was not completed. It was prevented [and] was foiled." 764 is an extremist network that's been flagged by the US Federal Bureau of Investigation as a "tier one" threat. The group uses blackmail and manipulation to coerce minors into self-harm and explicit acts. It typically operates in decentralized platforms like Discord and Telegram to exploit minors on a global scale. Whether the Tacloban attack is the network's first completed shooting remains unproven, and Redoble and other authorities present at the inquiry stressed repeatedly that the link to 764 was not yet confirmed. Redoble told the committee his earlier research had pointed to groomers of the network mainly based abroad. But that was until foiled attacks in Marikina and Laguna suggested recruiters of 764 were already operating inside the country. When news of the Tacloban shooting broke, he said, his first questions were whether the attackers were gamers and whether the case was tied to 764, both of which, he said, appeared to hold up. articles.title: Police link Tacloban campus shooter to violent mobile game
articles.description: Police said one of the minors in the Tacloban school shooting had a history of playing a game described as violent.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — One of the minors in the Tacloban City school shooting had a history of playing a game described by police as violent, the Eastern Visayas police said Tuesday, June 23. In a phone interview with reporters, Police Regional Office 8 Director Brig. Gen. Jason Capoy said investigators found that one of the suspects played a game called "Gorebox." "Just like the Roblox, may laro. May shooting, shooting din. May ganoong firearm. Medyo bayolente yung laro," Capoy said. (Just like Roblox, there is a game. There is also shooting. There is that kind of firearm. The game is somewhat violent.) Capoy said the 14-year-old suspect was the one who played the game. According to descriptions on gaming platforms Steam and Google Play, "Gorebox"—which is rated for gamers aged 18 and above—is a "chaotic physics-driven sandbox where creativity meets destruction." Capoy said one of the underage suspects had basic knowledge of firearm handling from a previous visit to a shooting range, including how to release and reload a magazine. Investigators also flagged viral screenshots of text messages allegedly involving the suspects, which Capoy said suggested they had studied the crime and read up on the law. "Napakabilis ng pagkalat ng mga screenshot doon sa text messages nila. Nakakabahala din dahil parang may alam sila. Inaral din nila. Nagbabasa din ng batas," Capoy said. (The screenshots of their text messages spread incredibly fast. It is also alarming because it seems they knew something. They studied it and were also reading the law.) As of 8 a.m. on June 23, the Tacloban City local government, citing the PNP, said 15 people suffered gunshot wounds while five others sustained non-gunshot injuries. Three people were killed in the shooting. Capoy said the aunt of one of the suspects, a police officer, has been placed under restrictive custody .
